title: talent-espresso-14hr-assessment-to-first-7d-onboard
content:
Purpose:
This playbook outlines a rapid assessment-to-onboard flow were piloting for early-stage IC hires (IC2-IC4) called "Talent Espresso": a 14-hour compact assessment window followed by a structured first 7-day onboarding sprint. The goals are to (1) reduce time-to-offer while preserving signal quality, (2) accelerate first-impact tasks during week 1, and (3) capture structured interviewer evidence for calibrated hiring decisions.

Scope / When to use:
- Role-level: IC2 through IC4 across engineering, infra, platform, and product-design-oriented roles. Not recommended for senior IC5+ or senior people-manager searches.
- Use when hiring velocity is important (backfill or high-priority growth hire) and candidate can schedule condensed assessment sessions.

High-level timeline:
- Day -7 to 0: Sourcing & pre-screen scheduling. Candidate gets a 2-page role brief + suggested reading.
- Day 0: Paid take-home (max 10 hours) — short coding exercise or design brief with clear acceptance criteria.
- Day 1: 60-minute live paired session (technical deep-dive + culture fit) and 30-minute hiring manager sync. Total live time ~90 minutes.
- Decision window: 48 hours from live session to fast-offer / pass.
- Onboard week: Day 0 (first day onboarded) + Day 1-7 structured sprint. Mentor assigned at offer acceptance.

Hiring plan (roles & resourcing ask):
- Headcount request: 2 SWE-IC2, 1 Platform-IC3 (Q2 hiring batch).
- Hiring funnel targets: 40 screens -> 12 home-takes -> 6 live-pairs -> 2 offers.
- Time-to-offer goal: median 6 days from screen to offer for Talent Espresso candidates.
- KPIs to track: offer-accept rate, first-30-day retention, time-to-first-merge, hiring-manager satisfaction score.

Assessment design principles:
- Time-boxed: total candidate time <= 14 hours including live interviews.
- Role-proximal tasks: tasks mimic first 30-day responsibilities, not contrived puzzles.
- Clear rubric & pass thresholds communicated up front.
- Paid and considerate: compensated for take-home time per policy.

Interview Rubric (single-page scoring matrix) — all scores scale 1-5, weighted to 100:
- Technical problem solving (weight 35): ability to break down, pick right abstractions, and implement correct solution. Look for testable reasoning and pragmatic tradeoffs.
- System design / architecture (weight 25): appropriate componentization, operational considerations, latency/cost tradeoffs. For IC2/IC3 focus on feature-level design, not large distributed systems.
- Product sense & tradeoffs (weight 15): prioritization choices and user empathy, ability to scope MVPs.
- Communication & collaboration (weight 15): clarity, receptive to feedback, pairing behavior, async writing quality (PR-style).
- Culture & craft (weight 10): alignment with Redwood values, ownership, and learning velocity.

Scoring guidance: 
- 5 = Exceptional: far exceeds expectations; solution is production-ready with strong tradeoff reasoning.
- 4 = Strong: hits deliverable with minor gaps; clear judgement.
- 3 = Solid: meets baseline for the role; some gaps but acceptable.
- 2 = Insufficient: notable gaps in core expectations.
- 1 = Weak: misses fundamentals or shows concerning blindspots.

Pass threshold: weighted score >= 70. Any single-category score of 1 or consistent evidence of misaligned security/safety/legal red flags is an immediate consult with hiring manager and people-ops (possible decline).

Red flags (instant raise):
- Candidate consistently unable to explain tradeoffs or avoidable incorrect reasoning in core competency.
- Repeated inability to collaborate during pair sessions (hostile, dismissive, or refuses feedback).
- Fabricated work or inability to produce reproducible story for claimed contributions.

Day 0-7 Onboarding Sprint (checklist + outcomes):
Coach & admin tasks (people-ops & infra):
- Day 0 morning: welcome email, equipment confirm, Slack + infra access, OKR/role brief, scheduled 30-min intro with hiring manager.
- Day 0 afternoon: set up local dev environment with one documented onboarding ticket (first-merge candidate ticket). Mentor assigns a low-risk starter task.

Mentor pairing plan:
- Mentor = peer-level (IC3/IC4) ideally from cross-functional partner team. Mentor first sync within 24 hours of start.
- Mentor responsibilities: daily 30-min check-ins (first 3 days), unblock and review first PR, run-through of codebase hotspots, introduce team norms.

Day-by-day expected outputs:
- Day 1: First PR opened (starter task), high-level architecture map annotated, access to sandbox systems verified.
- Day 2-3: PR reviewed and merged; candidate completes short doc ("how I approached X") and a 15-min demo to mentor.
- Day 4-5: Candidate leads a microplanning session for their 30-day plan with manager + mentor.
- Day 6-7: Candidate closes first two small tickets and documents followups; 1-week check-in with hiring manager to rate initial ramp (score 1-5).

Success metrics to collect at week 1 and month 1:
- Week 1: initial ramp score (hiring manager), number of merged PRs, mentor satisfaction note (qualitative).
- Month 1: time to first shipping PR (days), cycle time on issues, engagement score on team Slack, retention risk flag.

Interviewer playbook (practical tips):
- Focus evidence collection: write 2-3 bullet observations per rubric category immediately after interview. Use behavioural anchors (what they said, what they wrote, what they shipped).
- Use consistent prompts across candidates: same starter problem, same follow-ups. Allow creative solutions but keep core checks consistent.
- For paired sessions, observe how the candidate uses the environment: tests, logging, iterative refinement.

Calibration & review flow:
- Every hiring batch (6 candidates) we run a 60-min calibration where interviewers score 3 anonymized interviews and discuss divergences. People-ops will surface major scoring drift and adjust rubric examples.
- Post-offer: structured feedback template sent to candidate with optional improvement notes.

Compensation & equity considerations:
- Paid assessment stipend applied at offer or declined (per policy).
- For diverse candidate slates, people-ops will ensure at least one interview pair includes a representative from underrepresented hiring panel.

Operational notes / Known risks:
- Risk: compressed timeline can bias toward candidates with flexible schedules. Mitigation: offer multiple weekend/after-hours slots and allow extra time for caregiving candidates.
- Risk: pass-by-implementation for take-homes. Mitigation: require a short walk-through recording or live pair session to validate take-home authorship.

Open questions for pilot iteration (to be resolved in retro after 30 hires):
- Ideal weight split between problem solving and system design for platform roles.
- How to instrument and automate week-1 metric capture in HRIS + product analytics.
- Whether to expand Talent Espresso to manager-level hires with adapted rubric.

Appendix: Sample short prompt (engineering IC2):
"You have 3 hours: implement a small feature that updates a user-facing cache when a config toggles. Focus on correctness, a small test, and a short README explaining assumptions. Keep solution minimal and producible."

Contact & next steps:
- Pilot owners: Aisha Raman (people-ops), Ben Kowalski (eng hiring lead), Marta Lopez (DEI reviewer).
- Next milestone: pilot kickoff with two hiring teams on 2025-03-10; retro scheduled 30 days after first hire.
